text: Yeah, so MATIC network is a full blown proof of stake network and on the side chain, in order to participate in the side chain, that means whether you are a validator or whether you are a user. So the way to participate is Matic token. Like if you are a validator, like because you are validating what is happening in the network, you have to put a stake. And since we are a layer two, all of this stake goes on the Ethereum Mainnet. So on Ethereum Mainnet you have to put a stake and then you can become a validator. On Matic network, once you become a validator, you start participating into the validation of the network. You do a consensus amongst your other validators and then you put a checkpoint on Ethereum on which the validators earn the rewards because they are, if you are a user or a developer and you want to deploy smart contracts and everything, you don't need to stick. But then you have to pay the gas fees just like you have to pay on Ethereum, you have to Pay the gas fees in Ethereum token on the Matic network layer 2 sidechain, you have to pay the gas fees in MATIC tokens. So these are the two primary use cases of MATIC and the staking use case that I'm saying. So there can be 100 plus validators on the Matic layer 2 and eventually going into maybe thousands of validators. So you can initiate a validator node and then you can also ask people to delegate to you because not everyone can be a validator in the network. So if you are a normal, let's say token holder, what you can do is you can delegate to any of the validators. So we have a sticky UI where you can see who all are the validators and you can delegate to them. Now once you delegate to them the validator, because they are running the full infrastructure and all that, they might charge you a small commission fees on the rewards you get. And then that commission fees is basically their incentive. And then they have their own tokens also staked. So they make money on their own stake tokens plus the commission on the delegated tokens. And what you do is that the large part of the stake actually goes into the network. So it gets staked into the network. And due to that and these tokens which are staked into a network, let's say if you are a validator and then your validator node falters, let's say there's a long time it is not signing the consensus transactions or it actually has some malicious behavior, let's say double sign. So there is a slashing part also like which happens on Ethereum. So the Ethereum smart contracts which are connected to matic layer 2 sidechain so they will be able to detect that if somebody is doing like the consensus mechanism is designed in a way that it is able to detect that if some validator is having a malicious behavior and if there is a malicious behavior, there is a slashing that happens like your tokens are slashed basically on Ethereum minute if there's a malicious behavior or fraudulent behavior for that matter. So that stake actually contributes to the overall security of the network. And then a large part of the stake, basically the token supply gets staked into the network which is securing the network, basically essentially securing the network. And then the stakers actually get the rewards for participating in the network consensus. They also get to have the transaction fees once the you know that there are more and more transactions. So that's the basic idea.
